lexical_surface.syntax_whitespace: the explicit ASCII set HT, LF, CR, and space; VT, FF, and all non-ASCII whitespace are not syntax whitespace
lexical_surface.non_ascii_boundary_whitespace: rejected; no Unicode trimming is permitted
lexical_surface.identifier_domain: ASCII letters, ASCII digits after the first character, and underscore
lexical_surface.unicode_content: preserved byte-for-byte in supported opaque text and value atoms
lexical_surface.headers: schema, theory, instance, equation, rewrite, and named-constraint headers consume the complete header and accept zero or one trailing colon; module headers accept no colon; unrecognized constraint text containing a colon or no syntax whitespace is a named-header candidate
lexical_surface.qualified_fields: Relation.field is adjacent; syntax whitespace before or after the dot is rejected
lexical_surface.call_interiors: recursive type and refinement calls accept the explicit ASCII syntax-whitespace set immediately inside either parenthesis and around interior separators; VT, FF, and non-ASCII whitespace reject
lexical_surface.reversible_separator: @reversible requires one or more characters from the explicit ASCII syntax-whitespace set; attached and non-ASCII separators reject
lexical_surface.value_atoms: nonempty non-delimiter text may start with a digit and is preserved exactly without numeric canonicalization
lexical_surface.finite_lists: empty, interior-empty, and trailing elements are rejected; only the explicit empty set literal is an empty finite collection
lexical_surface.u32_tokens: nonempty ASCII digits only; no sign, interior whitespace, Unicode digits, or values above 4294967295
lexical_surface.declaration_introducers: physical-line declaration keywords include one literal ASCII space; general syntax whitespace applies only where the grammar owns a whitespace token

adversarial_matrix.accepted_parse_rule: compare independently normalized Rust and Lean ASTs
adversarial_matrix.accepted_typecheck_rule: run standalone Rust and Lean typecheck entry points and compare the declared result
adversarial_matrix.coverage: runner-validated generated Cartesian boundary cells for constraints, u32 tokens, rewrite Path forms, and recursive constructors

authority.lean_reconstruction: Lean reads the same exact UTF-8 source image and runs Axiograph.Axi.AxiV1.parseAxiV1 independently.
authority.compiled_ir_role: derived execution and citation substrate after canonical formation
authority.source_map_role: nonsemantic operational metadata outside this AST contract

exact_byte_anchor.bom: not part of the grammar and rejected as an invalid module header

ordering_note: No parser, normalized comparison view, compiler, or checker may sort these arrays. The AST uses separate top-level declaration-family arrays; the exact source bytes retain the complete cross-family textual order.

u32.surface: nonempty ASCII decimal digits without sign or whitespace

surface_forms.module: module Name; this must be the first non-comment, non-whitespace canonical header
surface_forms.line_comment: # or --; the first marker from left to right starts comment text
surface_forms.import: import Name; imports must immediately follow the module header and precede all sections
refinement_predicate: cardinality(Min|Max), where Min and Max are u32 values
constraints: at_most N Rel.src -> Rel.dst param (role, ...), where N is a u32 value
symmetric Rel where Rel.role in {Value, ...} on (left, right) param (role, ...); the guard field must be qualified
Name with an optional single trailing colon, followed by an indented opaque body
an unrecognized nonempty constraint family is preserved explicitly as ConstraintV1.unknown
a malformed recognized functional/at_most/typing/symmetric/transitive/key form is a parse rejection
surface_forms.equation: equation Name with an optional single trailing colon, followed by one indented lhs = rhs body
surface_forms.equation_value_types: checked PathExprV3 endpoint variables range over declared object types and declared relation objects in initial Rust, runtime Rust, and Lean checks; only object types have subtype edges
surface_forms.rewrite: rewrite Name with an optional single trailing colon, exactly one vars, lhs, and rhs field, and at most one orientation field; rewrite object variables name object types only
surface_forms.headers: schema, theory, instance, equation, rewrite, and named-constraint headers are all-consuming and accept at most one optional trailing colon; module accepts no colon
surface_forms.schema_header: schema Name:; the name is one identifier and the optional trailing colon occurs at most once
surface_forms.object_spacing: object Name uses exactly one ASCII space after object; an additional space or HT before Name rejects
surface_forms.finite_lists: leading, interior-empty, and trailing comma or pipe elements reject; the explicit empty set literal remains valid
surface_forms.role_kind_spacing: an explicit @kind must be separated from the role type by one or more characters from the declared syntax-whitespace set; attached forms reject
surface_forms.call_interior_spacing: relation, indexed, refined, eq, in, enum, key, cardinality, and predicate calls accept the declared ASCII syntax whitespace immediately inside either parenthesis and around interior separators
surface_forms.reversible_spacing: @reversible must be separated from the generator target by one or more HT, LF, CR, or space characters; attached, VT, FF, and non-ASCII separators reject
surface_forms.theory_key_spacing: theory-level key Relation(field, ...) permits ASCII HT/LF/CR/space before and inside parentheses and around commas; this is distinct from recursive refinement key(earlier_role|...)

leading, interior-empty, or trailing finite-list element around a comma or pipe

unsupported_forms.parse: accept and preserve every ordered field

theory constraint with an unknown relation/field; checked PathExprV3 equation with an unknown relation, incompatible inferred variable type, invalid composition, or unequal endpoints; duplicate equation name; or typed rewrite with an unknown type, endpoint, variable, relation, carrier pair, or incompatible endpoints

unsupported_forms.parse: not a language constructor or claim
